title: F5 warns of six critical BIG-IP flaws in the TMM data plane; hotfixes only
summary: F5 disclosed six critical stack-based buffer overflows in the BIG-IP Traffic Management Microkernel, CVSS 9.8, that can crash the data plane without logging in on specific virtual-server setups, including iRules and one APM policy. The report says they may allow remote code execution. F5 lists no exploitation. Fixes are engineering hotfixes only, with no workaround.
plain: F5 reported six serious flaws in its BIG-IP load balancers that an attacker with no login could use to crash the device, and possibly run code, on certain configurations.
exec: BIG-IP sits at the network edge of many large organisations; hotfix-only fixes mean teams must request builds rather than apply a routine update.
action: Check whether BIG-IP virtual servers use the iRules or the APM per-request policy named in the advisories, and request the engineering hotfixes from F5 (security notification K000164058, hotfix policy K4918); F5 lists no workaround.

sources.name: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, AV26-1178 (19 Nov)

key_findings: Six stack-based buffer overflows in the TMM data plane, CVSS 9.8 (v3.1) and 9.3 (v4.0).
Four reported by watchTowr, two found by F5; no exploitation listed in the advisories.

validation.note: Verify desk read The Hacker News (18 Nov) and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-1178 (19 Nov): both list the same six CVEs with engineering-hotfix fixes. CVSS 9.8, no workaround and no exploitation are stated by The Hacker News only (CCCS gives no CVSS and does not mention exploitation). F5 own portal (K000164058) did not load (JavaScript shell), not read.

review.note: Compared with The Hacker News, CCCS AV26-1178, GBHackers, Dailysecu: six CVEs, CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated TMM crash, may allow RCE, hotfix-only, no workaround, no exploitation listed, date 18 Nov
